newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese firms show 12% rise in interim profits.
newsitem.headline: Japanese firms show 12% rise in interim profits.

text.p: Interim earnings figures from nearly 400 major Japanese firms give an average increase in profit of nearly 12 percent, a corporate survey showed Thursday.
Wako Research Institute of Economics said the current profits of parent firms increased an average of 11.56 percent in the first half of the 1996/97 business year.
Current profit is pretax profit, which includes gains and losses made on securities investments and other non-operating activities.
Wako Securities Co.'s research arm based its figures on the interim parent current profit results of 397 companies.

It tracks 766 large companies, all of which have business years ending on March 31. The list does not include banks, brokerages or insurance firms and not all the companies listed have yet released their interim results.
The after-tax parent profits of the 397 firms increased 9.57 percent in the interim period compared with the previous year, while parent sales were up 4.71 percent, the survey said.
The parent current profits of car makers and car parts manufacturers jumped by an average of 78.8 percent, while those of oil companies dropped by an average of 59.59 percent, the survey said.
